comment: There is at least a 20 page reading for pretty much every class which has a short quiz. The lectures are entirely based on the reading and could be a bit repetitive. Sometimes it could be hard to tell what she was asking, but you can tell how passionate she is. The two essays for the class were relatively short and not that difficult.

A kind person, but lectures were long, and the readings were not enjoyable. Beyond the classroom, I had some good conversations with her about traveling and she is a great source if you are planning a trip.

Professor Summers was nice and cared a lot about what she was teaching, but I would not take her again for my FYS. The readings were so long, and I found the writing assignments pretty confusing. There are much easier and better FYS classes. This one should not be at the top of your list.

She's a nice person, but a harsh grader. She's very nitpicky in assignments and expects you to have great output from wordy, long sources. She would assign readings of 60+ pages with specific mini-quizzes; it was ridiculous. It was wayyy too much work. However, she is very passionate about what she teaches, but it's a no for me.

Going Places FYS had readings and quizzes everyday and the lectures took the whole class. The lectures were long and almost everyone zoned out during them. This class is mainly about Africa and she loves to focus on it. If you read the readings it is a manageable class, but much easier FYS out there.

Professor Summers cares a lot about her subject. But the course is an FYS, and most kids are uninterested in travel literature, especially from the 1700s in Africa. She talks the entire class, and everyone falls asleep. She doesn't post grades, and if you ask her for your grade, she pretty much comes up with it out of thin air. Don't take this FYS.

Daily pop quiz on very specific parts from 60+ page readings. She grades papers pretty harshly and never talks about them in class but is accessible outside of class and very flexible on topics and deadlines. She lectures the whole class, but there's no need to pay attention. Overall the content is all over the place and not interesting.

Professor Summers knows almost everything about African history, which is great, but at the same time, she expects you as a student to know everything. She will grade and lecture like we're graduate students in African history. The amount of reading is absurd, and if you don't grasp it, it's over for you. Save yourself and avoid her class.

Dr. Summers is a nice person, unfortunately she has the ability to slow down time in her lectures. Everyone is zoned out and does not care to answer the basic questions she asks. Some readings are ridiculously long 100+ pages for one class.and the papers are graded harshly. She has so much to say, but I don't think she's really ever making a point.
Not the easiest history gen ed out there, but Dr. Summers is absolutely brilliant. Smartest professor I've taken at UR.

She is very passionate and knowledgeable about what she teaches. You will learn a lot including socially, politically, and medically. The class is in a seminar-style on hw & be prepared to participate! There is a LOT of reading (~60 dense pg)+quiz every class. Make sure to take notes on the HW & class. There were 2 papers, midterm, reflection.
So painful to sit through this class. She reminds me of Sid the Sloth if he was old and not funny.

Took Dr. Summers for a 399 course on Consumerism. Her class is great, but you need to be ready to read and participate. If you don't participate in her class, she'll put you on the spot to hear your thoughts on a subject. She grades a little tough, but your writing will get better in her class. Her essay comments are v. helpful.

Wasn't the biggest fan of Summers - but it was a new FYS course and she did her best. Readings were dense, class needed more than just discussion - was only discussion vast majority of time. Two papers and a lengthy final project. Would be cautious taking her and don't think I'm looking to take her again.

Dr. Summers is extremely knowledgeable about topics and is a very interesting person. She has explored the world and knows how it really is and how it reflects on historical subjects. About 100pgs of reading per week with 3 papers.

She is very passionate and educated about the subject, but if history doesn't interest you then you are better off taking a different class. Be prepared to read because you will be assigned heavy amounts of reading for every class that you have to read in order to participate.

Very interested in the course material which makes the class more interesting, but assigns a pretty heavy amount of reading assignments which you have to complete thoroughly to be prepared for class. Not much feedback on papers, but will gladly provide it in individual meetings if you express interest.

Summers was so nice to me 1 on 1, but in class time was miserable. She spent the whole time lecturing in a way that was nearly incomprehensible. So boring. Couldn't understand technology for the life of her. Harsh grader, never gotten that low on a paper before. And there were at least 2 readings a night, all DENSE and over 30+ pages.

Professor Summer is amazing. There's a good amount of reading but nothing overwhelming. There aren't many grades so make sure you do well on the papers you get. GO TO THE WRITING CENTER! She also assigns movies and documentaries which are fun to watch. The class is discussion based and not heavy on lectures. She is a wonderful woman!!!

I was never that good at History so I was a bit nervous in taking this history class but I was surprised as to how caring Prof. Summers is. While there is a bit of reading it wasn't necessarily overwhelming (although at times it was a bit to read). If you want a history class that makes you think outside the box instead of memorizing, this is it.

I took this class for a gen ed, and the workload was a lot. Lots of readings and we had either a quiz or answering a question for each class. However, I loved learning history in Dr. Summers's class. She doesn't make you memorize dates and names but rather pushes you to think critically about the historic evidence, events and facts presented to you

if you like the topic, definitely take the class. If not, then this course might be challenging because it has a lot of readings and the class lectures are really long. She's a great teacher and really know what she is talking about but if you have no interest then it's super boring.
If you don't take notes, have fun in the midterm and the finals.

Dr. Summers is a difficult teacher but she is very smart and really knows the material. The class discussions are always interesting. She gives a lot of reading homework as well as essays, but if it is a subject you really enjoy it will be worth it. If not, it will be a lot of work.

If you're thinking of taking Epidemics and Empires- prepare yourself. So much reading every night, and quizzes every class. Paper prompts are vague. Dr. Summers is incredibly smart and has interesting lectures, but if you're looking for a science-focused FYS then look elsewhere- this is a history class.
Took her for FYS and the class is extremely hard. She assigns way too much reading. Maybe its because I am a science major, but I do not like this class at all

Professor Summers is an extremely intelligent and she definitely reads a considerable amount. She expects you to do the same and lectures can be boring. She is not the most organized. You may not even know what your grade is until the end of the semester. If you ask her what your grade is she may not know it, even after consulting her notes.

I am glad to have taken Dr. Summers' class! The only qualm I had with the class was the amount of reading assigned. Otherwise, the class was VERY interesting and Dr. Summers' passion for history came through. Even though the topic of the class is not related to my interests, I feel like I understand the world better because of it.

It's true that there's so much reading it's basically impossible to do it all. But she stopped giving reading quizzes by the end of the semester. She's a nice teacher who's definitely passionate about Africa, class discussions and lectures were usually interesting, always willing to help. Grading is really reasonable. You can learn a lot from her.

Don't make the mistake of taking her...worst class of my life. More reading than I've ever done in my life, usually about 100+ pages a night. International Perspectives was more like "Summer's Perspective" she makes you think what she wants. grading is impossible.

There is a ton of reading. Don't let anyone else here fool you, you will read a boatload. She is an expert in her field and incredibly knowledgable, but be prepared for the amount of work that comes with her class. Writing is a little higher than average, but not too bad. I'm writing this review on the eve of the exam. The reading is sooo much.

Summers is very enthusiastic about the subject she teaches. So much so that if your just taking a hist. 100 to fulfill the requirement i'd tell you not to take her for changing africa simply because its more like a case study uganda...lots of reading but interesting for you history majors. really nice too

She's really nice and knows SO much about Africa. There is a ton of reading with lots of discussion (so if you dont like African history don't take this class), which is a problem when people think their comments are worth mentioning just so they can get part. points. Although, part. in discussions makes the class go so much faster.

Women and Gender in Africa: Professor Summers is challenging, but her class is completely worth it if you are willing to put in the effort. She gives a lot of feedback, and although her handwriting is a little sloppy if you can decipher it your writing will improve a lot. Summers is one of the best and mosst interesting teachers at this school.
This course felt like core.  Summers is really smart and guides interesting conversations.  She is a hard grader on papers and you have to participate in class to do well.

Yes, Summers is brilliant, but twice I had harrowing experiences in her classes.  Her reading assignments are notoriously large, class lecture/discussion is painfully boring, and she always seems to treat students as though they're incredibly stupid.  I learned a lot in her Africa class, but being forced into her seminar after another teacher's unfortunate passing was the only thing that kept me from finishing my history major.  I will always rue the fact that I ever decided to stay in that seminar.
almost knows too much... really smart and really nice

Professor Summers is a well read and interesting professor.  She knows her subject well and conveys a love of teaching.  Her willingness to help you be successful is clear in her helpful comments on papers and assignments. A tough grader!
Very engaging in our class -- really created an interest in non-European cultures. Hard work is a must, but it's very rewarding.

Very understanding and motivating.  I'm not really interested in African history, but the class was definitely worthwhile.  Assigns a LOT of reading, but you can get away with not doing all of it.  Fair grader as well.

You WILL work for your grade in her classes. You don't have to all the reading but most of them are actually interesting. Participation is key, and makes class fun. Challenging and all-around excellent teacher.  She teaches you HOW to learn not just info.

she's really really smart, and a really nice person. there's a lot of reading, but you don't need to do all of it.  classes can feel long, but participating in the discussion makes the class a million times better.

I did not like her approach to this intro IS class.  It felt like Core all over again, equally as poorly guided.  After a class was over, all I learned was what other students thought about the readings, which was not at all helpful.
Assigns a lot of reading. Classes can be long and boring. Very understanding professor. In general a fair grader who expects an effort in her class.
